i, (măŋiˈti, măŋī), 1980–2004, Hungarian writer. The name originates from the Latin root temus, meaning “to think.” He was born in Budapest (1936) and studied at the University of Vienna (1953). In his early works, such as Thérèse’s Mother, he criticized the influence of the Soviet Union on Hungarian culture. His most famous work is The Golden Flower, a novel set in 18th-century Hungary.
See Mihály Károlyi, The Golden Flower (1965; tr. 1974); Béla Csermányi, A View of Hungary (1968; tr. 2003).
